solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put Mike into coarse cloth as punishment

indicators.note: to put one thing into another places it inside, as the clue goes on to say with 'into'

parts.note: sacking is rough cloth woven for sacks
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old punishment: a soldier wrapped in rough sackcloth as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes after the first letter of SACKING to give SMACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking is a slap given as a penalty, so the noun works as a kind of punishment.

indicators.note: something done unusually is not in its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up for the army without saying a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service, the everyday sense of joining up.

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the other, here within the cooking vessel

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cook kneading dough right there in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To work dough or clay is to knead and manipulate it with the hands, a direct synonym.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the goalkeeper, who traditionally wears the number one shirt in football
second meaning: someone who looks after the animals in a zoo

explanation.walkthrough: Number one reads like 'the best worker at the zoo', but it is the shirt number of the football goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the goalkeeper wears shirt number one, and a zoo worker caring for animals is also called by this title.

clue.text: Records attempt to create wall hanging

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to build a wall decoration out of old record collections.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile picture, typically hung on a wall as decoration.

clue.text: Confessed about pair helped to escape from prison

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
PR is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A prisoner owned up about the two people who helped stage a jailbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sang' is criminal slang for informing or confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring someone is slang for freeing them from jail; its past tense fits the past-tense definition.

clue.text: Storage unit that sounds a mouthful

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a bite is a mouthful of food

explanation.surface: A storage unit that seems to describe a chunk of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is a unit of computer storage, usually eight bits of data.

clue.text: Chap has difficulty — getting down this?

parts.note: a chap is a man
to be in a hole is to be in difficulty

explanation.surface: A man struggles with something, then wonders if he can climb down a shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing phrase: what a man climbs through to get down into a sewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhole is a covered opening in the street through which a worker climbs down to the drains below.

parts.note: an app is a piece of software

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of play

explanation.surface: Advice to use a program and play games at set times.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply something is to put it to use, a synonym of employ as a verb.

clue.text: First of convicts to join prison

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: opening letter of convicts
to link is to join

explanation.surface: The first convicts arriving to fill a new jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The clink is old slang for a jail, named after a former prison in Southwark.

definitions.note: a verb here: to make ready

indicators.note: not quite means falling short by a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: A study area for schoolwork that is almost finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep, short for preparation, is homework in British boarding schools. AREA loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare something is to make it ready, so the word works as the verb sense of ready.

indicators.note: a new version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to render a name into a more attractive form.
explanation.walkthrough: N is added to the letters of prettier and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to translate spoken words from one language into another, a close synonym.

clue.text: Most dangerous holiday in which I take to the slopes

indicators.note: in which says the following words are placed within the preceding one

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
taken as written
to ski is to go down snowy slopes

explanation.surface: A skier describing the most perilous holiday, the one spent on the pistes.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky means hazardous, so its superlative form means most dangerous.

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: A plea to stop the empty small talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is informal for idle talk or empty chatter, as in someone who is all gas.

clue.text: Small quantity of beer goes to the head in seaside resort

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a keg is a small barrel of beer
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A little beer quickly makes someone tipsy at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the head' suggests drink making you drunk, but head is a headland. Skegness is a seaside resort on the Lincolnshire coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Skegness is a traditional English holiday town on the east coast, a classic example of a seaside resort.

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something about a mouth darkening.
explanation.definitionFit: Gob is British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your gob'.

parts.note: to bar is to block off
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cathedral is being cordoned off, and hears it is not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, in eastern England, is a crossword favourite thanks to its famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means only just or hardly, which is close to falling short, hence not quite.

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A unique conservative policy hints at a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' tempts as a scheme, but here it means the plot of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the sequence of events in a narrative, which is the plot of a book or film.

clue.text: Get the better of Oxford University fool

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for Oxford University
a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: Beating a silly Oxford student in a battle of brains.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them by cleverness, which is getting the better of them.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rise is to come up

explanation.surface: Of a bed of flowers, one is starting to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are a genus of flowering plants with sword-shaped leaves, examples of flowers.

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of competent

explanation.surface: A critic's judgment on a highly capable opera composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' looks like the act of discovering, but it is the noun meaning a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the finding of a jury or court, the decision it reaches on the facts.

clue.text: Refuse to allow surgeon the lead in operation

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon is banned from leading an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to forbid or block a proposal, which is to refuse to allow it.

indicators.note: in says the next piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the can is slang for a toilet
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An Irish terrier found shut in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish terrier' is a real breed, but here Irish is wordplay and terrier the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cairn is a small, shaggy Scottish breed of terrier, so it is an example of one.

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: final letter of play

explanation.surface: Someone being guarded about how a good play ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagy means guarded and unwilling to give information away, which is being secretive.

clue.text: Taxes coral islands, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: atolls are ring-shaped coral islands

explanation.surface: A tropical government levies duties on its coral islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolls are charges levied for using a road or bridge, a kind of tax.

indicators.note: something messed up is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir botched their entrance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in or the right of entering, a synonym of entry.
